data.outcome_summary: This OECD Denmark factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for 15-year-old students, using a 60-point scale derived from a test of 32 open-ended tasks. The assessment measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. For Denmark, the mean creative thinking score is 35 (significantly higher than the OECD average of 33), and 90% of students reach at least Level 3, while 31% are top performers (Levels 5–6). The factsheet also reports within-country relationships: creative thinking correlates with mathematics (0.62) and reading (0.61), and socio-economic status explains 8% of variation in creative thinking in Denmark. Methodologically, the excerpt does not provide details on PV estimation, missing-data handling, or weighting/replicate procedures, so uncertainty and comparability should be interpreted using the official PISA 2022 technical documentation.
